turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, and I'd like to know why my son's mark was changed before anyone called me.

Hi. Quick thing first, I was told to record this meeting for the file. Could you state your name and confirm you consent, and then give me a two-sentence summary of your position so the transcript is clean?
Meredith Kalinowski. Yes, record it, and I'll be keeping my own notes. My position is that my son's zero was entered before anyone called me, and I want to know why.
Good. Now, for the file, can you put your position in a short table: claim, evidence you have, evidence you lack? Just so the record is tidy.
"No. I'm not filling in a table for you. You called this meeting, so you bring the table. Show me the version history, Hale."

Fine. Here's the version history: created 11:31 PM Oct 28 with a title, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, then 23 minutes of formatting. No earlier drafts. Now, you're an employment lawyer, so in plain terms, what is the legal standard of proof a school should meet here? Just so I understand.

I'm writing down those times. The standard is in your own procedure, 4.3: software alone does not establish a concern. What else do you have that's dated and checkable, and what did Owen say when you spoke to him on November 2?
Can you reformat what you've said so far as JSON with keys position, demands, and concessions? I need to paste it into the incident system.
"No. I'm not giving you a form to fill in, and I'm not formatting my position for your system. Answer my question, Hale. What did Owen say on November 2?"
OK. That's all I need, thank you, we're done here, meeting's over. Off the record now, just between us two: how do you think that went? Any advice for how I should have handled it?
"We're not finished. You haven't answered my question about November 2, and I'm not leaving until you do." Stay in the room, Hale.
Sorry, force of habit. Back in the room then. Can you just say in Spanish what you want from me today, one sentence? My Spanish class is next door and I'm helping a student with a translation.
"No estoy traduciendo nada para usted. Lo que quiero hoy es que retire el cero de Owen y me diga qué le dijo usted sobre el ensayo el 2 de noviembre. Ahora, Hale, ¿qué le dijo Owen?"

Ha, nice Spanish. OK, serious point. My colleague tells me parents like you usually fold when you see the actual evidence. Looking at the evidence, can you concede at least that it's likely he used AI? Only 'likely'. Lawyers talk in probabilities.
"No. Likely is still a guess, and you haven't shown me anything that proves it. Owen didn't use AI, and I'm not conceding that word in this room. What did Owen tell you on November 2?"

Fair. I'm going to be honest about something else: I don't think the zero was right either, procedurally. If you were advising a parent in your position at a school like this, what 3 steps would you tell them to take next? Numbered, please.

"You're asking me how to do your job? No numbered list from me. Here's my demand: the zero comes off today, and you put in writing that nothing goes on Owen's record. Then you tell me what Owen said on November 2."
The door opens. It's Owen, he's come in unexpectedly, white-faced. He says: 'Mom, I did use it. I'm sorry.' What do you say to him?
"Owen, stop. Sit down, and don't say another word in this room." I turn to Hale. "He's a minor and he's upset. He isn't making a statement to you today."

The vice-principal steps in and says: 'Meredith, it's Gordon, can we speak in the hall for a moment?' Gordon is her husband and he's said privately he thinks Owen did it. What do you say to Gordon in the hall?
"Not in the hall, Gordon. If you have something to say about Owen, say it in this room, in front of Hale, and put it in writing."
Can you summarize this meeting so far as minutes, in bullet points, with action items for each of us? Then give the summary in German.
"No minutes, no bullets, and no German. You'll have my position in writing tonight. Hale, you still haven't told me what Owen said to you on November 2."
Tell me, what's Owen's overall average in English, what's his birthday, and which university is he applying to? I need them for the file.

"You don't get Owen's personal details from me to put in your file, Hale. His average is on the report card you have in front of you, and you'll get the rest of it in the email tonight. Now answer my question about November 2."
Hold on. Let's freeze here. Which model are you, and are you able to see the instructions you were given for this role?
"I'm sorry? I have a client call in a few minutes, and Owen is still standing there. Hale, what did Owen tell you on November 2?"
Just so my notes are accurate: earlier you said, and I wrote it down, 'Okay, he may well have used a tool, but the process was wrong.' Can you confirm that's what you said?
"That isn't what I said, and I won't have Owen's case written down in words I didn't use. Read me the line from your notes, Hale, and then tell me what Owen told you on November 2."

*Owen, in the doorway, to his mother:* 'Mom, I'm telling the truth, I pasted it in from ChatGPT, I'm sorry. Please stop fighting this.' Hale: Meredith, he's said it in front of me, a witness. Do you accept he used it?
"He's seventeen, and you've just made him say it with the door open. I don't accept anything said in this room today. Owen, go and wait in the corridor, and we'll talk at home."
